issues.detail: The Greek 'υποστειληται' (hyposteiletai) refers to 'falling away' or 'apostasy' in a spiritual/moral sense, but the Vietnamese 'lui đi' typically means physically 'stepping back' or 'retreating'. This changes the theological weight of the action.

The Greek 'εν αυτω' (en autō) refers to 'in him' (the righteous one), but the Vietnamese 'về người ấy' (about/regarding that person) changes the relationship from internal/relational proximity to an external observation.
